rack: Standard alpine rack to 3in, doubles in common mid sizes

_raw.approach: Cedar Creek Trail ~5 miles from parking
_raw.land_manager: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee or Chelan Ranger District)
_raw.special_hazards: Glacier travel on approach; exposed rock climbing
_raw.seasonal_closures: Typically winter conditions Nov-May; check current conditions

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.notes: Not inside North Cascades National Park — this corridor is entirely Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District). No Mount Rainier-style climbing fee applies here.
access.rules: No climbing or wilderness permit required for day climbing. Dispersed camping capped at 10 days; no camping within ¼ mile of Cutthroat Lake; no campfires at dispersed sites; bear-resistant food storage required; dogs on leash ≤6 ft.
access.seasonal: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes gate-to-gate roughly early December–mid/late April; the entire Washington Pass corridor is car-inaccessible in winter.
access.landManager: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee or Chelan Ranger District)
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).

overnight_permit.where: Nothing to obtain for a night on the climbers' trails. The Early Winters valley campgrounds charge a nightly fee.
